newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan tax hike impact seen limited -- EPA official.
newsitem.headline: Japan tax hike impact seen limited -- EPA official.

text.p: The increase in Japan's consumption tax is likely to have only a limited impact on consumption, as expected, a senior official of the government's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said on Tuesday.

The official told Reuters that the agency expected the impact of the increase in the tax to five percent from three percent, which took effect on April 1, to be substantially smaller than in 1989, when the three-percent tax was first introduced.
Prior to the introduction of the consumption tax in April 1989, people rushed to buy consumer goods, causing a sharp drop in consumption in the months in and after April.
"Compared with 1989, the impact is not much," the official said.
"There was no panic buying ahead of the tax rise this time. People reacted relatively calmly to the tax increase."
Increased demand ahead of the consumption tax increase was seen in a limited range of products, such as cars, houses, electronics appliances and accessories.

A sharp increase in consumption of general consumer goods was only seen in the last three days of March, the official said. Department store sales in the last week of March rose about 40 percent from a year earlier.
In the whole of March 1989, department store sales showed a year-on-year increase of 35.5 percent. Sales the following month dropped 8.9 percent.
The EPA official the increase in department store sales this March was likely to be about 10 percent.
"The expected increase in sales in March is not so big as in 1989, so the drop in sales in the following months may not be much," he said.
He said sales in the first week of April appeared to have been bad due to the sales tax increase and bad weather.
"But sales seemed to be picking up last week," he added.
